what_it_does.name: azure-kubernetes
what_it_does.summary: Instructions, reference files, templates and two bundled sub-skills for planning, creating and running Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters with the Azure MCP server, az and kubectl. The base skill produces a recommended AKS cluster configuration that separates Day-0 decisions such as networking and API server access from Day-1 features, and covers SKU choice, security, observability, upgrades, node pools, reliability and cost, with focused workflows for pod rightsizing, VPA, the cluster autoscaler and Spot node pools. The azure-kubernetes-app-deploy sub-skill containerizes an existing app, generates a Dockerfile and Kubernetes manifests, validates them against Deployment Safeguards DS001-DS013 and deploys to an existing cluster, and the azure-kubernetes-automatic-readiness sub-skill assesses clusters or manifests for AKS Automatic compatibility and offers fixes as diffs. Use it to create, provision, design, secure or optimize AKS.

choose between AKS Automatic and Standard

rightsize pods and set up VPA, the cluster autoscaler and Spot node pools

assess clusters or manifests for AKS Automatic readiness

risks.risk: Aggressive cluster autoscaler tuning can evict critical workloads when PodDisruptionBudgets are missing.
risks.severity: High for aggressive tuning, by the author
risks.mitigation: set PDBs on critical workloads and confirm with the user before applying, stated in the files

risks.risk: Shorter scale-down timers can cause node reprovisioning after brief demand changes, adding provisioning latency.
risks.mitigation: use a less aggressive profile for workloads with frequent short scale cycles

risks.risk: Applied rightsizing patches can starve workloads of CPU or memory when they go to production unreviewed.
risks.mitigation: review patches, test in non-production first and get explicit user confirmation, stated in the files

risks.risk: Stateful or single-replica production workloads on Spot nodes lose availability, since Spot VMs evict with 30-second notice and PDBs do not prevent reclamation.
risks.severity: High for production stateful workloads, by the author
risks.mitigation: use Spot only for suitable workloads, keep multiple replicas and regular-pool capacity

risks.risk: VPA in updateMode Auto changes production pods without review.
risks.mitigation: start in Off mode, no Auto in production without testing and explicit user confirmation

risks.risk: Switching an existing cluster to Cilium is irreversible, and enabling NAP removes cluster stop and start support.
risks.mitigation: explicit approval before NAP enablement, disable NAP before the Cilium update

risks.risk: Deleting the old cluster after migration with az aks delete --yes cannot be undone.
risks.mitigation: only after the owner closes the rollback window, stated in the files

risks.risk: Whatever the latest Gateway API release serves is applied to the cluster, since the CRDs are installed from releases/latest without a pinned version.
risks.mitigation: none stated, C2 rates the kubernetes-sigs source as trusted

risks.risk: Secret values in a project's .env file can reach the agent's context, since port detection reads .env and .env.example for a PORT line.
risks.mitigation: partly, the base skill says not to request or output secrets

limitations: The base NAP readiness check assesses configuration eligibility only, and workload fit and cost analysis stay missing.
NAP can reduce cost when dynamic capacity fits workload demand, and savings are not guaranteed.
With only Metrics Server, rightsizing uses live data with no historical trends and low accuracy.
VPA recommendations need 24 or more hours of data collection.
The documented Azure MCP AKS surface offers cluster and node-pool reads only, with no readiness-assessment operation.
There is no documented in-place Standard to Automatic SKU switch, so migration needs a new target cluster and a workload move.
The bundled constraint spec is v1.2.0, and its rule counts are not proof of what a given cluster enforces.
DS009, no :latest tag, is not auto-fixable.
Preferred Spot affinity cannot guarantee scheduling capacity, and pods pinned to Spot stay pending when Spot capacity is unavailable.
A newly installed add-on skill may only become active in a new session or after a restart.
An IP exhaustion conflict may require recreating the cluster.

known_problems.problem: MCP tool call fails or times out
known_problems.workaround: verify az login, confirm the subscription with az account show and check the resource group
request a quota increase or select a different region or VM SKU
re-plan IP ranges, may require cluster recreation
enable --enable-oidc-issuer --enable-workload-identity and configure the federated identity
fix the Dockerfile, .dockerignore or dependency files and retry az acr build
remove partial resources with kubectl delete -f k8s/, fix and reapply

known_problems.problem: pods in CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending or OOMKilled
known_problems.workaround: check logs, ACR access with az aks check-acr, node capacity or raise the memory limit

known_problems.problem: jq or the bundled sanitizer unavailable
known_problems.workaround: use rendered manifests or an approved projecting host read, never raw cluster JSON

known_problems.problem: HTTP 401, 403 or 404 on Azure or Kubernetes reads
known_problems.workaround: run az login, grant a least-privilege read role, or verify the target names

known_problems.problem: uvicorn, Fastify or the Flask dev server bind to 127.0.0.1
Next.js ISR fails with EROFS on a read-only filesystem
